    Main theorems (statements) #

    Theorems A and B of the introduction, Theorem 11.7 (thm:final-basis), Corollary 5.5 (cor:away-from-two-basis), and Theorem 11.8(2) (thm:final-standardness).

    Throughout, k is algebraically closed and A is a finite-dimensional k-algebra, in the same universe (the general Auslander--Reiten theory works in one universe). "Characteristic different from two" is ringChar k ≠ 2.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.theoremB (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (A : Type u) [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (hbasic : IsBasicAlgebra A) (hA : IsRepresentationFinite k Aᵐᵒᵖ) (hchar : ringChar k ≠ 2) :
    IsStandard k A

    Theorem B (that paper; Corollary 5.5, cor:away-from-two-basis). Every basic finite-dimensional representation-finite algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two is standard.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.basic_hasNormedBasis (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (A : Type u) [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (hbasic : IsBasicAlgebra A) (hA : IsRepresentationFinite k Aᵐᵒᵖ) (hchar : ringChar k ≠ 2) :
    HasNormedMultiplicativeBasis k A

    Corollary 5.5(2) (cor:away-from-two-basis), existence part: a basic representation-finite algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two has a normed multiplicative basis. The standard equivalence of Theorem B identifies A with A₀ (restricting to the projective labels), and A₀ has a normed multiplicative basis by Proposition 4.14 and Corollary 3.3.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.theoremA_of_ringChar_ne_two (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (A : Type u) [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (hA : IsRepresentationFinite k Aᵐᵒᵖ) (hchar : ringChar k ≠ 2) :
    HasNormedMultiplicativeBasis k A

    Theorem A away from characteristic two (that paper; Theorem 11.7(1) for char k ≠ 2, via Corollary 5.5(2) and Lemma 2.1): the basic algebra eAe is a representation-finite full corner, it has a normed multiplicative basis, and Lemma 2.1 lifts it to A.
